dissent: One could defend 'not-applicable' as an honest verdict rather than a defect; it is scored as a defect because the module's stated purpose is auditing this exact fixed schedule, and the frame gates all semantic evaluation.

Append-index inference is structural (setup length 11, capture[4]==3, collect:0-2, append-0/1/2 requests); p_literal fixture bytes are not in the packet, so a fixture producing appends at indices 1-3 cannot be excluded by direct byte inspection, though it would contradict that arithmetic.
findings: Vacuous frame — o14-setup-delivery-implement.py SETUP (~L35-37) expects 'append:success:1:normal'@8, ':2:'@9, ':3:'@10. s_domain.py setup() under policy='pending' appends every record including the AttemptStarted record (~L63-71: attempt then append per record), and append() names actions 'append:<name>:<record-index>:normal' (~L57). boundary-01 requires append_log length 3 (attestation needs collected==range(capture[4]) with collect:0-2; spec fixed_prefix_length=11; prestage notes 'append-0/1/2' requests), so the real literals are 'append:success:0/1/2:normal'. _frame() (~L99-109) is therefore False for every genuine scale-eight-action-race case; every verdict is 'not-applicable'; status can never be 'supported' or 'counterexample'.

Corruption masked — all semantic comparisons are gated `and frame` (~L150-200: H3 literal/index/decision, H4 q_invoked, H5 relation flags, H8 pairs, differing_journal_fields). With the broken frame, wrong decisions, forged incarnation_pairs, or false done masks on real-domain evidence also yield 'not-applicable' rather than 'counterexample': the checker cannot discriminate corruption. Minimal correction: fix the three append literals; preferably treat present-but-wrong fields as failures independent of frame membership.

Unbound event schema — o14-setup-delivery-control-build.py ev()/states() (~L40-57) reconstruct post-states by guessing POST keys, embedded 'core'/'source_generation' keys, or len-2 tuples. The actual encoding (check.py run_history t.trace_event appends ~L73-81; t.restore in audit_case ~L96) lives in the unsupplied batch-07 identity module. Any mismatch turns each case/control into an 'unrestorable'/'no genuinely reachable witness' limitation — honest, but discrimination is then unproven. Bind the retained-event schema explicitly. run_controls' inspect_cases parameter would correctly flag the implement inspector (all_detected=False via F1), but the proposal never exercises that interop.

Secondary gaps — (a) control 'generation-coupling' accepts any earlier bound pair (bd), so a forged pair can launder a corrupted core generation; no compound 'forged-pair-satisfies-coupling' mutation exists (m_forge is caught only via pair-origin bookkeeping). (b) 'invocation-flag' records a missing q_invoked row field as check failure, conflating corruption with unrestorable evidence. (c) states() reconstruction work is uncharged; only the per-prefix loop calls charge.take(1).
limitations: Static review only; no code imported or executed and no observed run claimed.

batch-07 identity module (t.trace_event, t.restore, t.comparison, relation.compare, identity_audit) and p_literal fixtures are unsupplied; event-state and row schemas are inferred from use sites in check.py and boundary.py.
No acceptance or execution authorization implied; findings are correction targets for the transport gate.
summary: NEEDS_CORRECTION. The o14 checker is vacuous on its target domain: its literal SETUP frame rejects every genuine boundary-01 schedule and every semantic gate is frame-conditioned, so neither 'supported' nor 'counterexample' is reachable on real or corrupted evidence. The control build's premise tables (source-only set, local refusal reasons, a_audit mask arithmetic, semantic.bind pair schema, per-prefix charge.take) match the supplied originals and most mutations discriminate, but controls depend on an unverified retained-event encoding and leave a forged-pair coupling gap.
